instagram_caption:
🚨 The $170B Rocket and the $5B Crash — Southeast Asia’s Superapp Shakeout

From zero to headline valuations in a single decade: Sea (Shopee) soared from near‑zero market value in 2010 to a peak of about $170 billion in 2021. Grab jumped to ~$40B around its SPAC listing the same year before a steep correction. GoTo — the Gojek + Tokopedia merger — rode hype into a 2022 IPO near the mid‑teens (billions), then collapsed to single‑digit billions. Traveloka never hit the public fireworks, but quietly rebuilt its private valuation after the pandemic.

Here’s the dramatic arc: 2010–2016 was the ground game — ride hailing, payments, and local marketplaces. 2017–2019 saw venture and expansion capital flow into logistics and cross‑border e‑commerce. The pandemic (2020) accelerated Shopee’s GMV and Sea’s gaming/business segments — by 2021 the market crowned Sea the regional titan (~$170B market cap). But 2022–2023 brought macro shocks, advertising slowdowns, higher rates, and investor scrutiny of unit economics. Grab and GoTo corrected heavily; Sea cratered from its peak but later showed pockets of recovery.

Numbers to remember: Sea peak ≈ $170B (2021), Grab peak ≈ $40B (2021), GoTo public valuation ≈ mid‑teens $B (2022 IPO), GoTo trough ≈ $4–5B (2023). Traveloka’s private valuation drifted in the $2–4B range and is trending up again. The last two years in the chart (2025–2026) are marked estimates based on market trends and reported recoveries.

Which move surprised you most — the Shopee rocket or the GoTo crash? Drop your pick and why in the comments. I’ll pin the best explanation.
